info.name: Docker Store API (v1)
info.description:
E-commerce modular monolith: users, products, orders, notifications.

How to run:
1. Start the project: docker compose up --build -d
   (after pulling a change to db/init.sql, reset the database first: docker compose down -v)
2. If you changed PORT, ADMIN_EMAIL or ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, update the collection variables host, adminEmail, adminPassword.
3. Image uploads: in Postman Settings > General > Working directory, choose the project folder docs/test-files
   (or pick docs/test-files/sample-product.png by hand in the "image" field of the upload requests).
4. Run the whole collection in order (Collection Runner). Every request has tests.

Folder 4 is the access-control proof: another customer's order, actions outside your role,
missing and forged tokens are all rejected. Folder 8 shows the login attempt limit, folder 9 the notifications.

The collection registers fresh accounts on every run, so it can be run again without a reset.

item.name: 4. Access control (proof)
item.description: Every request here is an attempt to reach someone else's data or to act outside one's role. All must be rejected.

item.name: 5. Validation and errors
item.description: Bad input gets a clear 4xx with the unified error format, never a 500.

item.name: Upload a file that is not an image

request.description: docs/test-files/fake-image.png is a text file renamed to .png. The server checks the file's real content, not its name.

response.name: 400 INVALID_IMAGE
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INVALID_IMAGE","message":"Invalid image","details":[{"field":"image","message":"image must be a JPEG, PNG or WebP file"}]}}

response.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
response.body: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Invalid input","details":[{"field":"name","message":"name is required (1 to 200 characters)"},{"field":"price","message":"price must be a number from 0 to 99999999.99 with at most 2 decimals"},{"field":"stock","message":"stock must be an integer from 0 to 1000000"}]}}

item.name: Product id is not a UUID

response.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
response.body: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Invalid input","details":[{"field":"items","message":"items must be an array of 1 to 50 entries"}]}}

response.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
response.body: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Invalid input","details":[{"field":"items[0].product_id","message":"product_id must be a valid UUID"},{"field":"items[0].quantity","message":"quantity must be an integer between 1 and 100"}]}}

response.name: 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INSUFFICIENT_STOCK","message":"Not enough stock for this order","details":[{"field":"items","product_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","requested":50,"available":3,"message":"Only 3 left in stock"}]}}

item.name: Order id is not a UUID

response.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
response.body: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Invalid input","details":[{"field":"limit","message":"limit must be an integer between 1 and 100"}]}}

response.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR
response.body: {"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Invalid input","details":[{"field":"status","message":"status must be one of: pending, confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled"}]}}

item.name: 6. Status changes: admin
item.description: pending -> confirmed -> shipped -> delivered. Skipping a step or changing a final status is refused.

exec: pm.test('200, admin sees customer A\'s order', () => {

response.name: 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION","message":"Cannot change order status from confirmed to delivered","details":[{"field":"status","message":"Allowed next statuses: shipped, cancelled"}]}}

response.name: 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION","message":"Cannot change order status from delivered to cancelled","details":[{"field":"status","message":"delivered is a final status"}]}}

item.name: Customer A sees the new status
7. Cancel gives stock back
item.description: Limited Edition Watch has only 3 in stock. Cancelling an order returns its stock in the same transaction.

exec: pm.test('Fewer than 3 available (1 is reserved by the previous order)', () => {

response.name: 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INSUFFICIENT_STOCK","message":"Not enough stock for this order","details":[{"field":"items","product_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","requested":3,"available":2,"message":"Only 2 left in stock"}]}}

request.description: cancelled is final, so stock can never be returned twice.

response.name: 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION
response.body: {"error":{"code":"INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION","message":"Cannot change order status from cancelled to cancelled","details":[{"field":"status","message":"cancelled is a final status"}]}}

exec: pm.test('201: the cancelled watch went back to stock', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: Admin cancels it (restores stock for the next run)
8. Login attempt limit
item.description: After 5 failed logins for the same IP + email within 15 minutes, login is refused with 429, even with the right password. Uses a fresh account each run.

item.name: Wrong password 6 times: the 6th is blocked

request.description: The pre-request script sends 5 wrong passwords first; this request is attempt number 6.

exec: body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email: pm.collectionVariables.get('emailRL'), password: 'wrong-password' }) },

response.name: 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
response.body: {"error":{"code":"TOO_MANY_REQUESTS","message":"Too many failed login attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."}}

request.description: Blocked means blocked: guessing the password now would not help an attacker either.

response.name: 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
response.body: {"error":{"code":"TOO_MANY_REQUESTS","message":"Too many failed login attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."}}

item.name: Other accounts from the same IP still work

request.description: The limit is per IP + email, so one attacked account does not lock everyone out.

item.name: 9. Notifications
item.description: Every order change creates a notification for the customer who placed the order. Customers only ever see their own.
